messages:
maya: Heads up — after the v7.3 canary rollout we saw a ~2.1x p99 latency jump on a subset of hosts. Not across all racks. looks tied to a tokenizer tweak + new kernel selection path.
jordan: Repro steps? which model variant and quant path?
maya: Model: openllm-v2-768 q4f16 + new tokenizer v2. Tokenizer change increased avg subtokens per prompt from 1.8 -> 2.6. Kernel tracer shows a lot more small-batch kernel switches.
liam: pinging the rollout summary: deploy-bot: Canary rollout for model openllm-v2-768 (rev a1b2c3) completed at 2026-03-18T09:12Z. 10% traffic.
sasha: I pulled traces from the affected hosts, attaching a snippet:
```
profiler: kernel_select: aten_gemm16 (prev) -> aten_smallmat (now)
batcher: avg_batch_size: 4.2 -> 2.1
kvcache: hit_rate: 0.77 -> 0.68
cpu->gpu memcpy count increased by 3.
```
dani: That batch size drop is bad — looks like batching heuristic flipped to prioritize latency but with smaller sequences the kernel decider prefers small-mat kernels that are much less efficient on our GPUs (high kernel launch overhead).
jordan: Any noisy neighbors or tenant correlation?
maya: Yes — noisy-tenant-17 traffic aligns. They sent many short prompts (chat API debug session). Prefetcher seems to evict KV entries more aggressively when seqlen spikes, causing more KV misses for other tenants.
liam: Can we pin kernel selector back to previous heuristic for the canary? Or force quant fallback path?
sasha: Quick mitigation: 1) rollback tokenizer change on canary 2) pin kernel policy to prefer aten_gemm16 when avg_batch_size < 8 but avg_seq_tokens > 32 3) increase KV prefetch retention threshold. Implementing now.
maya: Rolling rollback for canary + kernel pin; will monitor.
liam: For longer term: need to add a seq-len distribution check in rollout gating. If tokenizer increases subtokens by >15% for the same prompts, block kernel-autoselect until we rerun perf bench.
dani: Also add a small synthetic harness: run 1k short prompts + 500 mixed seqlen on each canary host to measure batcher knee before shipping tokenizer or kernel changes.
jordan: Agree. Also we should surface per-tenant short-prompt rate spike alarm to detect noisy-cheap-chat usage early.
maya: Canary rollback applied. p95/p99 trending back down (observed p99 drop from 480ms -> 230ms on affected hosts). Will keep canary at 0% until we validate fixes. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Canary rollback executed for openllm-v2-768 (rev a1b2c3) at 2026-03-18T09:29Z.
sasha: Filing a postmortem ticket and adding a checklist for kernel-selector experiments.
dani: I'll add a unit test in the batching harness to simulate tokenizer subtoken inflation.
maya: Thanks all — follow-ups: jira INF-3347 (rollback verified), INF-3348 (kernel gating + perf harness), INF-3349 (tenant noisy-rate alert).
jordan: Nice quick response :rocket:
